title: Students and youth strike across Croatia over living costs

tea.why: Protesters are striking over high living costs, unaffordable housing, and a lack of transparency in job applications.
tea.want: Affordable housing, better living conditions for youth, and transparent job application processes.
tea.changed: Nov 20, 2026: Education Minister Radovan Fuchs accused strikers of being anarchists and announced unexcused absences.

summary: High school students and university students across Croatia launched a nationwide all-day boycott of classes as part of the International Youth Strike initiative, which spans more than 25 European countries. A student representative stated that the participants organized independently to protest living costs, unaffordable housing, and systemic challenges that hinder youth from building a future in the country. Education Minister Radovan Fuchs criticized the actions, labeling the participants as anarchists involved in politicization, and warned that students skipping classes would receive unexcused absences.
demands: Better conditions to encourage youth to stay in Croatia
response: Education Minister Radovan Fuchs accused the strikers of being anarchists participating in politicization, argued that student measures are sufficient, and announced unexcused absences for students who miss school.

updates.text: High school students and university students across Croatia were called to a full-day boycott of classes as part of the Youth Strike.
Education Minister Radovan Fuchs criticized the strikers as anarchists and threatened unexcused absences for missing classes.
